components.name: ACE Step 1: Define the innovation package
components.description: Specify the core technology, the doctrine/operational practice required to exploit it, and the organizational changes required. An MMI is a system, not just a device.

components.name: ACE Step 2: Identify demonstration point (t0)
components.description: Mark the first use that reveals the innovation full strategic potential to the international system. This starts the diffusion clock.

components.name: ACE Step 3: Code FI and OC of the innovation
components.description: Rate FI (1-5) and OC sub-scores (1-5). Use the first-mover transformation depth as the OC benchmark. Store sub-scores separately.

components.name: ACE Step 4: Profile each actor capacity
components.description: Rate FI capacity (GDP, defense budget, procurement), OC capacity (org age vs t0, experimental R&D, task-focus breadth), and conceptual capacity (Adamsky) separately.

components.name: ACE Step 5: Compute fit and predict path
components.description: Compare requirement vectors to actor capacity vectors; assign one of the five response paths; derive adoption probability and time band; include demand-side control variables.

components.name: ACE Step 6: Derive system-level forecast
components.description: Project diffusion speed, adopter concentration, first-mover advantage duration, arms-race or stability dynamics, and instability risk from adopter/non-adopter imbalance.

components.name: ACE Step 7: Multi-method empirical test
components.description: Many potential adopters: quantitative logit/probit. Few, organizationally complex cases: qualitative process tracing. Link to evidence nodes with provenance.

components.name: Apply 5 Whys Analysis
components.description: Use iterative questioning to drill down from symptoms to fundamental causes

components.name: Create Fishbone Diagram
components.description: Map out all potential causes using cause-and-effect visualization

components.description: PWS methodology framework: Systems Analysis

components.name: Data
components.description: Symbols representing properties of objects and events; raw observation. Example: 'It rained 3mm.'

components.name: Information
components.description: Processed data made useful; answers who/what/where/when. Example: 'It rained 3mm more than average.'

components.name: Knowledge
components.description: Know-how; the application of data and information, conveyed by instructions. Example: 'When it rains more than average, flooding follows.'

components.name: Understanding
components.description: Appreciation of why; conveyed by explanations; the synthesis tier. Example: 'Deforestation upstream removed the natural water barriers.'

components.name: Wisdom
components.description: Evaluated understanding; deals with values and judgment; effectiveness (right goal) over efficiency; the long term. Example: 'We need reforestation AND flood defenses.'

components.name: WHY Phase
components.description: Understanding phase - questioning status quo and excavating root causes

components.name: WHAT IF Phase
components.description: Exploring phase - imagination and possibility exploration

components.name: HOW Phase
components.description: Acting phase - transforming ideas into actionable plans

components.name: Domain Generation
components.description: Generate 5-10 candidate domains before filtering. Mine four sources: Experience, Education, Curiosity, and Intersections. Quantity over quality at this stage.

components.name: Domain Evaluation
components.description: Score each domain 1-5 on three criteria: Interest, Knowledge, Research Accessibility. All three must be present. High interest with low knowledge is fantasy. High knowledge with low access is frustration.

components.name: Domain Validation
components.description: Test top domains with real research: Literature Scan (prior art, gaps, key players), Stakeholder Check (reachable people), and Scope Test (multiple problems, clear boundaries, manageable).

components.name: Domain Finalization
components.description: Commit with confidence: craft domain statement using template [Activity/Field] for [Stakeholder/Context] in [Setting/Condition]. Create one-sentence pitch, problem inventory, and 30-day action plan.
